note: Most common Estonian and Lithuanian calendar names by official bearer counts (Statistics Estonia; Registrų centras TOP 50). Stories are scoped to their own country calendar. Source URLs are research/provenance metadata only and are never displayed in the widget.

records.name: Margus
records.facts_used: Estonian form of Marcus (Roman praenomen, probably from Mars); name day 25 April = markusepäev, folk name äkksurmapäev and field-work taboo; translatio of St Mark relics from Alexandria to Venice 828/829, portal mosaics, 1968 partial return to the Coptic Church.
records.reason: Uncited et.wiki claim that Margus is eestipärane not used.

records.name: Sirje
records.facts_used: Possibly from sinisirje (blue-feathered), folk song Sinisirje linnukene, possible Kalevipoeg association; Mägiste suggested it in 1929; also in LV calendar; Kapp opera Tasuleegid (libretto Rummo after Bornhöhe Tasuja), premiere 21 July 1945 in Gloria Palace, role Sirje (soprano), Stalin Prize 1946.
records.reason: Phrased to be true for LV bearers (history of the name, LV calendar entry). 1950s popularity remark omitted. Sirja not added (Finnish variant; the Mägiste claim is not literally true for it).

records.name: Kristjan
records.facts_used: Estonian/Slovene form of Christian < Latin Christianus; ten Danish kings named Christian; Kristjan Jaak Peterson (Christian Jakob Petersohn, b. Riga 14 March 1801, d. 1822 aged 21, theology in Tartu, maarahva laulik, 14 March = Native Language Day).
records.reason: LV-only Kristjans/Kristjānis not added.

records.name: Ülle
records.facts_used: Feminine of Ülo; Nordic Names links it to ülev; 1930s revival of old and new Estonian names with Ülo named; Kauksi Ülle (civil name Ülle Kauksi, b. 1962 Võru, Võro writer, began writing unaware she wrote in Võro, first collection Kesk umma mäke 1987).
records.reason: Uncited et.wiki claim of a 13th-century Old Estonian male name Ülle dropped. No claim that surname-first order is a Võro custom (not sourced).
records.next_steps: Find a primary source for the reported 13th-century Old Estonian male name Ülle.

records.name: Urmas
records.facts_used: Origin unsettled; BTN possible dialect urm frost/catkin; Finnish farm name at Koski (Turku province), also a surname there; later used in Estonia, also in place names; Linnankoski (real surname Peltonen) lived at Koski, named a son Urmas, character Urmas leader of the Mervi in the play Kirot.
records.reason: Son birth year 1906 (fi.wiki only) and play year (1907/1908 conflict) omitted.

records.name: Piret
records.facts_used: Estonian form of Birgitta (BTN) < Bridget < Irish Brighid, Celtic *Brigantī the exalted one; Birgitta of Sweden; name day 1 Feb = St Brigid of Kildare / Imbolc; Suur Tõll legends: wife Piret, brother Leiger, son Noor Tõll; legends collected to 1961 published 1963; 1980 animated film Suur Tõll (Rein Raamat, Jüri Arrak).

records.name: Kristi

records.name: Merike

records.name: Rasmus

records.name: Jaanus

records.reason: All facts verified in the listed opened sources.

records.name: Siim
